newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply down at slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply down at slow trade.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate extended earlier falls to close down 130 basis points at 26.75 percent due to light dealing amid ample market liquidity, traders said.
Traders pointed out that in addition to an injection by Banco de Mexico, government spending of some 3.7 billion pesos increased liquidity during the session.
Banco de Mexico injected 2.316 billion pesos by auctioning a three-day credit which it assigned at 27.71 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 150 basis points to 27.50 percent.
Other traders said secondary rates fell ahead of expected falls in inflation in the coming months.
"Rates are moving ahead of time, and are thus falling too quickly. We expected rates to return to a downward trend, but they're jumping the gun," another trader said.
Another explanation proferred was that rates fell due to speculation by dealers who took advantage of slow trade to dump paper.
"Volume was very thin, so it was easy for those with paper to bring rates down, especially if they had a surplus of paper," a trader said.
Total credit maturities expected for Monday were a hefty 9.534 billion pesos, which traders said could push rates up once more.
